materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure introduces a material change in the charge-off policy for consumer vehicle loans. Specifically, it adds a condition that loans are charged off 'when the borrower's ability to pay cannot be validated' and explicitly states they are charged off at 'estimated fair value less expected disposal costs'. The 2023 policy charged off at 'collateral values' upon 120 days past due or repossession. The addition of the 'ability to pay' validation trigger and the explicit definition of charge-off value (fair value less disposal costs) represents a change in the company's recognition and measurement methodology for credit losses.
materiality_analysis.key_change: Addition of ability-to-pay trigger for vehicle loan charge-offs

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit Card and Unsecured Revolving Loan Accrual and Charge-off Policies
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit cards and other unsecured revolving loans are not subject to non-accrual policies and continue to accrue interest until charged off at 180 days past due (DPD). Specific details regarding these charge-off policies are provided in a subsequent section.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose that credit card and unsecured consumer loans continue to accrue interest until charged off. However, C explicitly states that these loans are generally not subject to non-accrual policies, whereas BAC notes they are not reported as nonperforming loans while accruing. Both companies charge off these unsecured credit card loans at 180 days past due. BAC also specifies triggers for earlier charge-off such as death, bankruptcy, or fraud (within 60 days), which C mentions in a separate detailed schedule but aligns with in D077.

sentences.text: Credit card and other unsecured consumer loans are charged off when the loan becomes 180 days past due, within 60 days after receipt of notification of death or bankruptcy or upon confirmation of fraud.
These loans continue to accrue interest until they are charged off and, therefore, are not reported as nonperforming loans.
Credit cards and other unsecured revolving loans generally are not subject to non-accrual policies and continue to accrue interest until charged off at 180 DPD.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company charges off unsecured installment loans at 120 days past due (DPD) or within 60 days of bankruptcy notification, while unsecured revolving and credit card loans are charged off at 180 DPD. Loans secured by non-real estate collateral are written down to estimated value less selling costs at 120 DPD, whereas real estate-secured loans are written down at 180 DPD, with specific exceptions for non-foreclosure decisions and bankruptcy filings.
comparisons.comparison: This disclosure confirms the specific charge-off timing for unsecured revolving loans and credit card loans is 180 days past due (DPD) for C, matching BAC's 180-day threshold. Like BAC, C also charges off these unsecured loans within 60 days of notification of bankruptcy filing if earlier. This disclosure does not explicitly address the accrual status during this period, which is covered in C's D072.

sentences.text: Credit card and other unsecured consumer loans are charged off when the loan becomes 180 days past due, within 60 days after receipt of notification of death or bankruptcy or upon confirmation of fraud.
• Unsecured revolving loans and credit card loans are charged off at 180 DPD, or if in bankruptcy, within 60 days of notification of filing by the bankruptcy court, if earlier.

comparisons.peer_topic: Nonaccrual Loan Criteria and Interest Treatment
comparisons.peer_summary: Loans are placed on nonaccrual status when collection of principal and interest is probable not to occur, triggering reversal of accrued interest and cash-basis recognition or balance reduction; credit card loans accrue interest until paid or charged off, and are considered past due when contractual payments are missed.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS disclose that credit card loans accrue interest until charged off. GS explicitly states that credit card loans are not placed on nonaccrual status, similar to BAC's statement that they are not reported as nonperforming loans. This confirms a shared treatment of credit card receivables as accruing assets distinct from other non-performing consumer loans.

sentences.text: These loans continue to accrue interest until they are charged off and, therefore, are not reported as nonperforming loans.
Credit card loans are not placed on nonaccrual status and accrue interest until the loan is paid in full or is charged off.

comparisons.peer_topic: Exemption for credit card loans from nonaccrual status
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit card loans are generally exempt from nonaccrual status per regulatory guidance, allowing interest and fees to continue accruing until charge-off or full payment.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose that credit card loans are exempt from nonaccrual status and continue to accrue interest until charged off or paid in full. JPM explicitly attributes this to regulatory guidance, while BAC describes the operational outcome (not reported as nonperforming, accrue interest).

sentences.text: These loans continue to accrue interest until they are charged off and, therefore, are not reported as nonperforming loans.

As permitted by regulatory guidance, credit card loans are generally exempt from being placed on nonaccrual status; accordingly, interest and fees related to credit card loans continue to accrue until the loan is charged off or paid in full.
